doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Hollywood's reaction and Mancini's Peter Gunn
summary: Mandel was passed over for an Oscar nomination because the old guard disliked jazz, while Mancini's Peter Gunn the same year helped crack the ice.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So what was the reaction that that score got?
And you got an Academy Award nomination or didn’t?
Sure didn't, got frozen right out, Hollywood did not take very kindly to jazz in those days. The old guard especially Dmitri Tiomkin and those people did not like something like this come along.

Did not. The guys like Alex North, David Raksin, Hugo Friedhofer, they were very enthusiastic, but the real old bunch – you know I was one of the interlopers, they didn’t care to know about people like Hank Mancini and me in the late 50s, --not yet.
The irony was that that same year was the year that Mancini started doing the, Peter Gunn, scores for television.
He was doing Peter Gunn the same time I did, I want to Live!
And how much did that really crack the ice as far as jazz oriented writing?
Helped a whole lot, it really did. Hank was very good with it too.
